::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Sept 17th 1878  
**From:** Elderfield, Otterbourne, Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS Mrs Clare Roels
:::

My dear [Christabel](people/person_329.qmd)

The [Packet](organizations/other_52.qmd) will be happy to take [Cherry](other_books/otherbook_902.qmd) cut down when [Heriot’s Choice](other_books/otherbook_878.qmd) is over.  I am afraid it will last a long time – for I never can succeed in getting in two chapters of Heriot’s Choice-  Our pupil teachers have had a paper sent in from Salisbury training college for religious examination, saying 2nd class – [Alice Misselbrook](people/person_1257.qmd) 8, [Harriet Godwin](people/person_2316.qmd) 18, but whether this means no from the top or number of marks we in our inexperience do not know.  The [mistress](people/person_156.qmd) has been nursing her sick husband at Portsmouth for a fortnight, and they have kept school by themselves with good success -  the children have all been wonderfully good.  I believe the poor man is dying, but he is in Haslar Hospital and Mrs Bishop has come back to be sent for any time.[^1]  The [new master](people/person_513.qmd) promises well.  I hope your parish troubles will prove to be an eruption throwing off ill blood.  How often a worry comes after one has had a special pleasure

your affectionate
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: Possibly Matilda Bishop (b. Great Bookham 1831/2), an elementary school teacher and a widow in Otterbourne at the time of the 1881 census.  Her husband, a ship’s steward, was at sea in 1871.  However this may be a different couple.
